new_theorem.statement: For one original-coordinate hub h and leaf block A_II=D+sum lambda_k v_k v_k^T with D diagonal, let c=A[I,h], W=[v_1,...,v_r,c], G=W^T W>0, U=WG^{-1/2}, and rho be the Pluecker probability that two determinant-weighted (r+1)-coordinate bases of U are disjoint. Then ||p_Q||_infinity <= ((r+2)/r) exp((r+1)/(r+2)) [rho det(G) prod |lambda_k|]^(-1/(r+2)), uniformly over arbitrary A_hh,A_hJ,A_IJ,A_JJ and affine terms; same coefficient times |L| for intervals. This branch has a continuous density.
new_theorem.mechanism: Use the exact physical-hub Jacobian and Fresnel reduction from newest-Claude Theorem H, whiten the augmented curvature/star frame, replace the natural leverage gate by determinant-weighted entropy Brascamp-Lieb under disjoint Pluecker bases, then integrate the |t|^{-(r+2)/2} characteristic envelope directly.
no_hidden_assumptions: no probability squaring / square-root small-ball conversion

strict_n3_application.construction: One hub, star vector c flat on 256 leaves, curvature vector v1 with squared weights 0.6 plus 100 copies 0.004, second curvature vector v2 flat on a disjoint 256-leaf support; diagonal cancellations make every physical diagonal zero; curvature scalings make two positive curvature eigenvalues exactly 1.

small_rho_output.statement: For d=r+1, some d-coordinate Pluecker basis supports a unit active mixed direction with outside coordinate energy <= rho^(1/d). For r=2 this is a three-physical-coordinate localization witness.
small_rho_output.classification: structural localization alternative, not itself a density bound

designated_partner.application: Two flat disjoint grouped slopes plus the same heavy one-curvature vector; delta=1, pdet=1, rho=0.6334222412109375, lambda>=1, giving ||p||_infinity<4.964 on a target-valid strict-N3 matrix with spectrum containing +1,-1,+1,-1,+1.
